24	# Cerne Constitution
25	
26	## Core Principles
27	
28	### I. Product Source of Truth
29	`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
30	authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
31	functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
32	order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
33	reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
34	API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
35	Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
36	technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
37	`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
38	this repository.
39	
40	Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
41	backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
42	product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
43	stable.
44	
45	### II. Fixed Technology Stack
46	The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
47	using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
50	text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
51	the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
52	HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
53	and charting — are open implementation decisions.
54	
55	Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
56	architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
57	built by different contributors or at different times.
58	
59	### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
60	The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
61	documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
62	(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
63	backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
64	semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
65	NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
66	a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
67	`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
68	carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
69	header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
70	(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
71	marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
72	NEVER be committed.
73	
74	Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
75	scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
76	narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
77	credential leakage.
78	
79	### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
80	`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
81	spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
82	MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
83	exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
84	documentation MUST be in English.
85	
86	Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
87	checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
88	prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
89	preserving the product's voice.
90	
91	### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
92	Code MUST follow the folder convention:
93	```
94	lib/
95	  core/
96	  features/
97	    <feature>/
98	      data/
99	      domain/
100	      presentation/
101	```
102	The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
103	NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.
104	
105	Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
106	layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
107	portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.
108	
109	## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)
110	
111	These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:
112	
113	- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
114	  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
115	  loading indicator.
116	- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
117	  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
118	  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
119	- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
120	  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
121	- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
122	  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
123	- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
124	  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
125	- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
126	  target.
127	- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
128	  80% test coverage.
129	- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
130	  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
131	  `design_tokens.dart`.
132	- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
133	  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
134	  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
135	  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).
136	
137	## Scope & Delivery Boundaries
138	
139	- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
140	  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
141	- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
142	  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
143	  entry.
144	- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
145	  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
146	  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
147	  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
148	    `design_tokens.dart`.
149	  - Implementing extension features.
150	  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
151	  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.
152	
153	## Governance
154	
155	This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
156	instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
157	review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
158	considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
159	artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.
160	
161	**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
162	describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
163	accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
164	single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
165	Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.
166	
167	**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
168	- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
169	  redefinition.
170	- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
171	  guidance.
172	- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.
173	
174	**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
175	Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
176	RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.
177	
178	**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

## Scope & Delivery Boundaries

- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.

**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.

**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
  redefinition.
- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
  guidance.
- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.

**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

1	# Feature Specification: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `002-biometric-auth-vault` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-11
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault: Protect access to the user's data with a Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier, validated on the device, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF03) and section 10 (parameters), matching the prototype states 'Tela 0.1 — Biometria', 'Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial', 'Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha'. No biometric endpoint exists on the backend; the biometrics preference is stored via PATCH /account/settings, and the session is renewed with POST /auth/refresh or POST /auth/login after passing the barrier. Depends on F000 (session, login). Do not implement features of later units, extension features, or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-11
14	
15	- Q: During first-time PIN setup, if the user opts into Face ID/Touch ID and the `PATCH /account/settings` call to save `biometricEnabled` fails (timeout, no connection, etc.), should that block the user from reaching Home/Chat, or should the app proceed locally and let the write resolve/retry in the background? → A: Proceed locally and retry in the background — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already work regardless of backend reachability; first-time setup does not block on this write succeeding, consistent with the local-first philosophy of FR-002 and FR-015 (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).
16	
17	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
18	
19	### User Story 1 - Unlocking the app with Face ID / Touch ID (Priority: P1)
20	
21	A returning user who has already set up the vault opens the app (cold launch) or brings it back from the background after a long pause. Before anything from their journal or chat becomes visible, they are asked to confirm their identity with Face ID or Touch ID. On success, the app proceeds exactly as it would have without the vault.
22	
23	**Why this priority**: This is the barrier itself — the entire reason the unit exists. Without it, no access protection exists at all.
24	
25	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app on a device with biometrics enrolled and the vault already configured, confirming the biometric prompt appears before any data is visible, and confirming a successful scan proceeds into the app's normal session routing.
26	
27	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
28	
29	1. **Given** a device with a PIN already configured and Face ID/Touch ID enabled, **When** the app is cold-launched, **Then** the biometric prompt appears before any journal or chat content is shown, and a successful scan proceeds to the app's existing session routing (Home/Chat or login, depending on session validity).
30	2. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more, **When** it resumes, **Then** the biometric prompt appears again before the previous screen becomes visible or interactive.
31	3. **Given** the app was sent to the background and brought back in under 5 minutes, **When** it resumes, **Then** no authentication is required and the user sees exactly the screen and state they left.
32	
33	---
34	
35	### User Story 2 - Biometric failure falls back to PIN (Priority: P1)
36	
37	A user's fingerprint or face is not recognized (bad lighting, wet finger, a scan error). Rather than being stuck, they are immediately offered their PIN as an alternative and can still get into the app.
38	
39	**Why this priority**: Explicit acceptance criterion in the requirement — a failed biometric read must never lock the user out, since biometric sensors fail routinely under normal conditions.
40	
41	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a biometric failure (denied, cancelled, or not recognized) and confirming the PIN screen appears with an error message, then confirming a correct PIN still unlocks the app.
42	
43	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
44	
45	1. **Given** the biometric prompt is shown, **When** the scan fails or is not recognized, **Then** the PIN entry screen appears showing the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", without any other interruption.
46	2. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters the correct 4-digit PIN, **Then** the app unlocks and proceeds normally.
47	3. **Given** the PIN screen shown after a biometric failure, **When** the user enters an incorrect PIN, **Then** the error state remains, the entered digits are cleared, and the user can try again with no limit that locks them out of the app entirely.
48	
49	---
50	
51	### User Story 3 - Setting up the PIN for the first time (Priority: P2)
52	
53	Right after a user's very first successful login or sign-up on a device, before they can use the app, they are asked to choose a 4-digit PIN and confirm it. This PIN becomes the fallback that always works, whether or not biometrics are set up.
54	
55	**Why this priority**: Every later unlock (Story 1 and 2) depends on a PIN already existing; without this step the vault has nothing to fall back to.
56	
57	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by signing up or logging in for the first time on a device with no PIN configured, confirming the create-PIN screen appears before Home/Chat, and confirming a matching confirmation proceeds while a mismatched one does not.
58	
59	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
60	
61	1. **Given** a user has just completed their first successful login or sign-up on a device with no PIN configured yet, **When** that happens, **Then** they are asked to enter a new 4-digit PIN and then re-enter it to confirm, before reaching Home/Chat.
62	2. **Given** the PIN confirmation step, **When** the re-entered PIN matches the first entry, **Then** the PIN is saved on the device and the user proceeds to Home/Chat.
63	3. **Given** the PIN confirmation step, **When** the re-entered PIN does not match, **Then** the user sees a clear message and is returned to entering a new PIN, without the mismatched PIN being saved.
64	4. **Given** the device supports Face ID or Touch ID, **When** PIN setup completes, **Then** the user is offered the option to also enable biometric unlock, and their choice is saved as their biometrics preference.
65	
66	---
67	
68	### User Story 4 - Recovering access via full login (Priority: P3)
69	
70	A user who cannot pass biometrics or does not remember their PIN taps a visible link on the vault screen and is taken to the regular email/password login, regaining access that way instead of being stuck.
71	
72	**Why this priority**: A safety valve for the barrier itself; it depends on the vault screen (Story 1) existing, and reuses login machinery that F000 already built, so it carries the least new risk of the four stories.
73	
74	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "usar e-mail e senha" from the vault screen and confirming it leads to the existing login screen, where submitting valid credentials proceeds into the app.
75	
76	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
77	
78	1. **Given** the vault screen (biometric or PIN) is shown, **When** the user taps "usar e-mail e senha", **Then** they are taken to the existing login screen.
79	2. **Given** a user who reached login this way, **When** they submit valid credentials, **Then** they proceed into the app the same way a first-time login would.
80	
81	---
82	
83	### Edge Cases
84	
85	- A device has no biometric hardware, or no fingerprint/face enrolled at the OS level: the vault shows the PIN screen directly as the only method, without attempting or showing a fingerprint prompt first.
86	- The app process is killed by the operating system while backgrounded (not merely suspended): the next launch is treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault, regardless of how little time has passed.
87	- A user disables biometrics at the OS level (outside the app) between sessions: the next vault appearance falls back to PIN entry directly, with no error shown for the missing biometric capability.
88	- The background timer sits exactly at the 5-minute boundary: fewer than 5 minutes elapsed never re-prompts; 5 minutes or more always does.
89	- The app is killed mid-way through first-time PIN setup (Story 3) before confirmation completes: relaunching resumes the PIN setup flow rather than leaving the user in an unusable, PIN-less state.
90	- Repeated incorrect PIN entries: never produce a hard lockout of the app; the user can always retry or fall back to "usar e-mail e senha".
91	- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.
92	
93	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
94	
95	### Functional Requirements
96	
97	- **FR-001**: The system MUST require the user to pass a local authentication check — Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN — before showing any of the user's journal, chat, or account data, on every cold launch and on every resume from the background, whenever a PIN has already been configured on the device.
98	- **FR-002**: The system MUST perform this authentication entirely on-device; no biometric data and no PIN value may be sent to, or validated by, the backend.
99	- **FR-003**: When biometrics are enabled and available on the device, the system MUST attempt Face ID/Touch ID first; when biometrics are unavailable (no hardware, nothing enrolled, or disabled), the system MUST present PIN entry as the method shown, without attempting a biometric prompt.
100	- **FR-004**: When a biometric attempt fails or is not recognized, the system MUST immediately offer PIN entry as an alternative, together with the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", and MUST NOT lock the user out of attempting authentication again.
101	- **FR-005**: The PIN entry MUST use a 4-digit code entered on a numeric keypad with backspace, showing progress across 4 dots as digits are entered.
102	- **FR-006**: The vault screen MUST offer a visible link ("usar e-mail e senha") that leads to the existing email/password login screen, for cases where neither biometrics nor the PIN can be used.
103	- **FR-007**: When the app is sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more have elapsed, the system MUST require the authentication barrier again before the previously visible screen becomes visible or interactive.
104	- **FR-008**: When the app is sent to the background and brought back in under 5 minutes, the system MUST NOT require re-authentication, and MUST resume exactly the screen and state the user left.
105	- **FR-009**: The 5-minute background timeout MUST be a fixed value with no user-facing setting to change it.
106	- **FR-010**: When the barrier is triggered after a background timeout, the system MUST preserve the state of the screen underneath it and restore that exact state once authentication succeeds.
107	- **FR-011**: The first time a user completes a successful login or sign-up on a device with no PIN configured, the system MUST require the user to create a 4-digit PIN and re-enter it to confirm, before any further screen is reachable.
108	- **FR-012**: If the confirmation PIN does not match the first entry, the system MUST reject it with a clear message and let the user set a new PIN, without saving the mismatched value.
109	- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, the system MUST let the user optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID unlock as part of first-time PIN setup, and MUST persist that choice as the account's biometrics preference through the backend.
110	- **FR-014**: Persisting the biometrics preference MUST reuse the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit, not a separate or ad hoc HTTP call. If that call fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the failure MUST NOT block PIN setup from completing or the user from reaching Home/Chat — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already govern unlocking regardless of backend reachability, and the preference write is left to resolve or retry through the existing failure-handling path.
111	- **FR-015**: Passing the local barrier MUST NOT by itself constitute backend authentication; the app MUST continue to rely on the session machinery already established (silent renewal, or a full login if the session can no longer be renewed).
112	- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any later-delivered requirement (RF01, RF02, RF04 through RF10), including building the Settings screen; any biometrics control beyond first-time setup is out of scope.
113	- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT implement any extension feature (manual tags, action plans, persona selection).
114	- **FR-018**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its contract, or its configuration in any way.
115	
116	### Key Entities
117	
118	- **Device PIN**: A 4-digit secret stored only on the device, created once during first-time setup and checked locally on every subsequent unlock attempt; never transmitted to or validated by the backend.
119	- **Vault Lock State**: Whether the current app session is currently locked or unlocked, and the timestamp of the last time it was unlocked — used to decide whether a resume from the background falls under or over the 5-minute threshold.
120	- **Biometrics Preference**: An account-level flag (`biometricEnabled`) indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's enrolled unlock method; read and written through the backend's account-settings endpoint, but never the thing that performs the actual biometric check.
121	
122	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
123	
124	### Measurable Outcomes
125	
126	- **SC-001**: 100% of cold launches and background resumes of 5 minutes or more show the authentication barrier before any user data becomes visible.
127	- **SC-002**: 100% of resumes from the background under 5 minutes skip authentication and restore the exact prior screen state.
128	- **SC-003**: A user whose biometric attempt fails can always reach their data via PIN in the same session — 0 cases where a biometric failure alone ends in the user being unable to proceed.
129	- **SC-004**: A new user completes first-time PIN setup (create + confirm) successfully in a single guided flow, with no path that leaves the device without a usable PIN.
130	- **SC-005**: Across a full lock/unlock cycle triggered by a background timeout, the screen state underneath (scroll position, visible content) is unchanged in every observed case.
131	
132	## Assumptions
133	
134	- The prototype extract shows no screen dedicated to first-time PIN creation, distinct from "PIN inicial" (first entry) and "PIN após falha" (entry after a failure). This unit reuses the same 4-digit keypad component for a create-then-confirm flow the first time a device has no PIN, since no separate enrollment screen is documented.
135	- A dedicated toggle to change the biometrics preference later (outside of first-time setup) belongs to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit; this unit implements the account-settings read/write path for `biometricEnabled` but not that screen's UI.
136	- The vault only engages once a PIN has been configured on the device. A device with no PIN yet (first-ever app use before any account exists) is unaffected by this unit and continues straight to F000's existing login/sign-up flow; PIN setup is triggered immediately after that flow's first success (Story 3).
137	- "Usar e-mail e senha" reuses F000's existing login screen unmodified; this unit adds only the navigation link to reach it from the vault.
138	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay built by F000 for a genuinely expired backend session is unaffected by this unit and continues to route to the login screen as F000 built it; routing it back through the vault instead is left to the unit that owns live in-session behavior (RF07), consistent with not implementing later units' functionality.
139	- No maximum-attempt lockout is implemented for PIN entry; repeated incorrect attempts show an inline error and allow retrying indefinitely, with "usar e-mail e senha" always available as a fallback.
140	- Device biometric availability (hardware present, something enrolled, not disabled) is read from the platform's own biometrics API; this unit does not reimplement that detection.
141	- The Face ID/Touch ID prompt is triggered automatically as soon as the vault screen with biometrics enabled appears (standard platform behavior), not only after a tap; the fingerprint circle and "Toque para desbloquear" act as a manual retry affordance for when the OS prompt was dismissed or cancelled, consistent with User Story 1's requirement that the prompt appear before any data is shown on cold launch.
142	- When a user disables biometrics at the OS level between sessions (see Edge Cases), this unit does not call the backend to flip `biometricEnabled` to false; the account-level preference is only ever written during first-time setup (FR-013) in this unit, and keeping it in sync with later out-of-band OS changes is left to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit, consistent with the existing assumption that a dedicated toggle belongs there.
143

### Edge Cases

- A device has no biometric hardware, or no fingerprint/face enrolled at the OS level: the vault shows the PIN screen directly as the only method, without attempting or showing a fingerprint prompt first.
- The app process is killed by the operating system while backgrounded (not merely suspended): the next launch is treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault, regardless of how little time has passed.
- A user disables biometrics at the OS level (outside the app) between sessions: the next vault appearance falls back to PIN entry directly, with no error shown for the missing biometric capability.
- The background timer sits exactly at the 5-minute boundary: fewer than 5 minutes elapsed never re-prompts; 5 minutes or more always does.
- The app is killed mid-way through first-time PIN setup (Story 3) before confirmation completes: relaunching resumes the PIN setup flow rather than leaving the user in an unusable, PIN-less state.
- Repeated incorrect PIN entries: never produce a hard lockout of the app; the user can always retry or fall back to "usar e-mail e senha".
- The `PATCH /account/settings` call that saves the biometrics preference during first-time setup fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response): PIN setup still completes and the user still reaches Home/Chat; the write is not retried synchronously as part of the setup flow.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The system MUST require the user to pass a local authentication check — Face ID, Touch ID, or PIN — before showing any of the user's journal, chat, or account data, on every cold launch and on every resume from the background, whenever a PIN has already been configured on the device.
- **FR-002**: The system MUST perform this authentication entirely on-device; no biometric data and no PIN value may be sent to, or validated by, the backend.
- **FR-003**: When biometrics are enabled and available on the device, the system MUST attempt Face ID/Touch ID first; when biometrics are unavailable (no hardware, nothing enrolled, or disabled), the system MUST present PIN entry as the method shown, without attempting a biometric prompt.
- **FR-004**: When a biometric attempt fails or is not recognized, the system MUST immediately offer PIN entry as an alternative, together with the error message "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN", and MUST NOT lock the user out of attempting authentication again.
- **FR-005**: The PIN entry MUST use a 4-digit code entered on a numeric keypad with backspace, showing progress across 4 dots as digits are entered.
- **FR-006**: The vault screen MUST offer a visible link ("usar e-mail e senha") that leads to the existing email/password login screen, for cases where neither biometrics nor the PIN can be used.
- **FR-007**: When the app is sent to the background and brought back after 5 minutes or more have elapsed, the system MUST require the authentication barrier again before the previously visible screen becomes visible or interactive.
- **FR-008**: When the app is sent to the background and brought back in under 5 minutes, the system MUST NOT require re-authentication, and MUST resume exactly the screen and state the user left.
- **FR-009**: The 5-minute background timeout MUST be a fixed value with no user-facing setting to change it.
- **FR-010**: When the barrier is triggered after a background timeout, the system MUST preserve the state of the screen underneath it and restore that exact state once authentication succeeds.
- **FR-011**: The first time a user completes a successful login or sign-up on a device with no PIN configured, the system MUST require the user to create a 4-digit PIN and re-enter it to confirm, before any further screen is reachable.
- **FR-012**: If the confirmation PIN does not match the first entry, the system MUST reject it with a clear message and let the user set a new PIN, without saving the mismatched value.
- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, the system MUST let the user optionally enable Face ID/Touch ID unlock as part of first-time PIN setup, and MUST persist that choice as the account's biometrics preference through the backend.
- **FR-014**: Persisting the biometrics preference MUST reuse the single typed-failure network call path already established by the foundation unit, not a separate or ad hoc HTTP call. If that call fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the failure MUST NOT block PIN setup from completing or the user from reaching Home/Chat — the local PIN and the on-device biometric toggle already govern unlocking regardless of backend reachability, and the preference write is left to resolve or retry through the existing failure-handling path.
- **FR-015**: Passing the local barrier MUST NOT by itself constitute backend authentication; the app MUST continue to rely on the session machinery already established (silent renewal, or a full login if the session can no longer be renewed).
- **FR-016**: This unit MUST NOT implement the functional behavior of any later-delivered requirement (RF01, RF02, RF04 through RF10), including building the Settings screen; any biometrics control beyond first-time setup is out of scope.
- **FR-017**: This unit MUST NOT implement any extension feature (manual tags, action plans, persona selection).
- **FR-018**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its contract, or its configuration in any way.

### Key Entities

- **Device PIN**: A 4-digit secret stored only on the device, created once during first-time setup and checked locally on every subsequent unlock attempt; never transmitted to or validated by the backend.
- **Vault Lock State**: Whether the current app session is currently locked or unlocked, and the timestamp of the last time it was unlocked — used to decide whether a resume from the background falls under or over the 5-minute threshold.
- **Biometrics Preference**: An account-level flag (`biometricEnabled`) indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's enrolled unlock method; read and written through the backend's account-settings endpoint, but never the thing that performs the actual biometric check.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of cold launches and background resumes of 5 minutes or more show the authentication barrier before any user data becomes visible.
- **SC-002**: 100% of resumes from the background under 5 minutes skip authentication and restore the exact prior screen state.
- **SC-003**: A user whose biometric attempt fails can always reach their data via PIN in the same session — 0 cases where a biometric failure alone ends in the user being unable to proceed.
- **SC-004**: A new user completes first-time PIN setup (create + confirm) successfully in a single guided flow, with no path that leaves the device without a usable PIN.
- **SC-005**: Across a full lock/unlock cycle triggered by a background timeout, the screen state underneath (scroll position, visible content) is unchanged in every observed case.

## Assumptions

- The prototype extract shows no screen dedicated to first-time PIN creation, distinct from "PIN inicial" (first entry) and "PIN após falha" (entry after a failure). This unit reuses the same 4-digit keypad component for a create-then-confirm flow the first time a device has no PIN, since no separate enrollment screen is documented.
- A dedicated toggle to change the biometrics preference later (outside of first-time setup) belongs to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit; this unit implements the account-settings read/write path for `biometricEnabled` but not that screen's UI.
- The vault only engages once a PIN has been configured on the device. A device with no PIN yet (first-ever app use before any account exists) is unaffected by this unit and continues straight to F000's existing login/sign-up flow; PIN setup is triggered immediately after that flow's first success (Story 3).
- "Usar e-mail e senha" reuses F000's existing login screen unmodified; this unit adds only the navigation link to reach it from the vault.
- The "Sessão expirada" overlay built by F000 for a genuinely expired backend session is unaffected by this unit and continues to route to the login screen as F000 built it; routing it back through the vault instead is left to the unit that owns live in-session behavior (RF07), consistent with not implementing later units' functionality.
- No maximum-attempt lockout is implemented for PIN entry; repeated incorrect attempts show an inline error and allow retrying indefinitely, with "usar e-mail e senha" always available as a fallback.
- Device biometric availability (hardware present, something enrolled, not disabled) is read from the platform's own biometrics API; this unit does not reimplement that detection.
- The Face ID/Touch ID prompt is triggered automatically as soon as the vault screen with biometrics enabled appears (standard platform behavior), not only after a tap; the fingerprint circle and "Toque para desbloquear" act as a manual retry affordance for when the OS prompt was dismissed or cancelled, consistent with User Story 1's requirement that the prompt appear before any data is shown on cold launch.
- When a user disables biometrics at the OS level between sessions (see Edge Cases), this unit does not call the backend to flip `biometricEnabled` to false; the account-level preference is only ever written during first-time setup (FR-013) in this unit, and keeping it in sync with later out-of-band OS changes is left to the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit, consistent with the existing assumption that a dedicated toggle belongs there.

see data-model.md Device PIN / Biometrics Preference. No SQL/NoSQL local database is introduced.

111	## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Biometric failure falls back to PIN (Priority: P1)
112	
113	**Goal**: A failed, cancelled, or unrecognized biometric attempt immediately offers PIN entry with
114	the exact fallback message, never locking the user out; a correct PIN still unlocks.
115	
116	**Independent Test**: Force a biometric failure; confirm the PIN screen appears with the error
117	message, then confirm a correct PIN still unlocks the app.

119	### Tests for User Story 2

122	
123	### Implementation for User Story 2
124	
125	- [ ] T035 [P] [US2] Create `VerifyPinUseCase` in `lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase.dart` — thin delegation to `repo.verifyPin(pin)`

134	## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Setting up the PIN for the first time (Priority: P2)
135	
136	**Goal**: The very first successful login/sign-up on a device with no PIN leads straight into
137	create-then-confirm PIN setup, with an optional biometrics opt-in, before Home/Chat is reachable; a
138	mismatched confirmation is rejected without saving; a mid-setup kill resumes setup on relaunch.
139	
140	**Independent Test**: Sign up fresh on a device with no PIN configured; confirm the create-PIN
141	screen appears before Home/Chat; a matching confirmation proceeds, a mismatched one does not.

143	### Tests for User Story 3

145	- [ ] T039 [P] [US3] Write `SavePinUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/save_pin_usecase_test.dart` against a fake `VaultRepository`, verifying it delegates to `repo.savePin(pin)`
146	- [ ] T040 [P] [US3] Write `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/save_biometrics_preference_usecase_test.dart` against fake `VaultRepository`/`BiometricsPreferenceRepository`: the local mirror is written synchronously *before* the network call fires (research.md R6); a `Left` result from `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save` is discarded and does not throw or propagate — the usecase always completes

148	### Implementation for User Story 3

152	- [ ] T043 [US3] In `VaultBloc`, handle `pinSetupRequired` entry: create-PIN step holds the first 4-digit entry only in bloc memory (never written to storage yet — data-model.md); confirm step does a pure string-equality check — on match, call `SavePinUseCase` then, if `checkBiometricCapability() == available`, emit a biometric opt-in step; on mismatch, emit a clear mismatch message and return to the create-PIN step with nothing saved (FR-012) — depends on T021, T041, T042
153	- [ ] T044 [US3] In `VaultBloc`, handle `BiometricOptInToggled` by calling `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, then transition to the unlocked/complete state regardless of its outcome, proceeding to Home/Chat (FR-013, FR-014) — depends on T043
154	- [ ] T045 [US3] Build the PIN-setup UI states in `VaultPage` — create-PIN step, confirm-PIN step with mismatch message, and (when biometric capability is available) the biometrics opt-in prompt — reusing the shared `PinKeypad`; on gatekeeper-mode completion, `context.go(AppRoutes.home)` — depends on T022, T023, T044
155	- [ ] T046 [US3] In `lib/features/auth/presentation/pages/login_signup_page.dart`, change the non-reauth `AuthStatus.authenticated` branch from `context.push(AppRoutes.home)` to `context.push(AppRoutes.vault)` — depends on T024
156	- [ ] T047 [US3] Extend `VaultBloc` tests in `test/features/vault/presentation/bloc/vault_bloc_test.dart`: `pinSetupRequired` → matching create/confirm → PIN saved, biometric opt-in available → `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` invoked → unlocked/complete; mismatched confirm → mismatch message, create step re-entered, `savePin` never called; a `pinSetupRequired` re-open before confirmation completes (process killed mid-setup) re-enters the create step rather than any unlocked/Home state, since `hasPinConfigured()` is still `false` (Edge Cases) — depends on T043, T044
157	
158	**Checkpoint**: All of Stories 1–3 are independently functional — the full vault core loop (setup → unlock → fallback) works end to end.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## Phase 6: User Story 4 - Recovering access via full login (Priority: P3)
163	
164	**Goal**: A visible "usar e-mail e senha" link on the vault screen leads to the existing
165	email/password login, regardless of whether the vault is showing the biometric or PIN state.
166	
167	**Independent Test**: Tap "usar e-mail e senha" from the vault screen; confirm it leads to the
168	existing login screen; submitting valid credentials proceeds into the app.
169	
170	### Implementation for User Story 4
171	
172	- [ ] T048 [US4] Add a visible "usar e-mail e senha" text link to both the biometric-prompting and PIN-entry UI states in `VaultPage`, dispatching `UseEmailPasswordRequested` (FR-006) — depends on T028, T037
173	- [ ] T049 [US4] In `VaultBloc`, handle `UseEmailPasswordRequested` by triggering `context.push(AppRoutes.login)` from `VaultPage` (no bloc state change needed beyond the navigation side effect) — depends on T048
174	- [ ] T050 [US4] Write a widget test in `test/features/vault/presentation/pages/vault_page_test.dart` confirming the "usar e-mail e senha" link is present and triggers a push to `AppRoutes.login` from both the biometric-prompting and PIN-entry states — depends on T049
175

179	
180	## Phase 7: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns
181	
182	**Purpose**: The constitution/quickstart gates that span every story above.
183	
184	- [ ] T051 [P] Run `fvm flutter analyze` and resolve any `always_use_package_imports`/lint findings under `lib/features/vault/`
185	- [ ] T052 [P] Run `test/architecture/domain_purity_test.dart` and confirm it still reports 0 violations with `lib/features/vault/domain/` included (RNF06)
186	- [ ] T053 Run `fvm flutter test --coverage`, extract `lib/**/domain/**` via `lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info`, and confirm ≥80% coverage with `lib/features/vault/domain/` included (RNF07)
187	- [ ] T054 Execute quickstart.md's manual verification on the iOS Simulator for Stories 1–4 and its edge cases: no-hardware/not-enrolled/OS-disabled-between-sessions shows PIN directly with no error; the exact 5-minute boundary; app killed mid-setup resumes setup; app killed while backgrounded is treated as cold launch; offline during the biometrics-preference write still completes setup and reaches Home/Chat
188	
189	---
190	
191	## Dependencies & Execution Order
192	
193	### Phase Dependencies
194	
195	- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
196	- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup (T003 for the route constant) — BLOCKS all user stories.
197	- **User Stories (Phase 3–6)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
198	  - US1 and US2 (both P1) should be done first — US2's "biometric fails → PIN" handler extends the
199	    same `VaultBloc` branch US1's biometric-success handler lives in (T027/T036 both touch
200	    `vault_bloc.dart`), so doing them in sequence avoids rework, even though each is independently
201	    testable once done.
202	  - US3 (P2) extends the same bloc/page with the `pinSetupRequired` branch — independent of US1/US2's
203	    code paths (different `VaultEntryMode` branch) but shares the file.
204	  - US4 (P3) only adds a link + navigation handler on top of UI states US1/US2 already built (T028, T037).
205	- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four stories being complete.
206	
207	### Within Each User Story
208	
209	- Tests before/alongside implementation (written to fail first, per the template's convention).
210	- Domain usecases before bloc wiring; bloc wiring before the page UI that reads it.
211	- Story complete (bloc + page + test) before moving to the next priority.
212	
213	### Parallel Opportunities
214	
215	- T002, T003 (Setup) in parallel.
216	- T004, T005 (entities), T010 (design token), T007 (second repository interface) in parallel within Foundational.
217	- T009, T014, T017 (test files) can be written in parallel with each other once their respective implementation task lands.
218	- T025/T026 (US1 usecase + its test) in parallel with T034/T035 (US2 usecase + its test) — different files, both depend only on Foundational.
219	- T039/T040/T041 (US3 usecases + tests) in parallel with each other.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## Parallel Example: Foundational Phase
224	
225	```bash
226	# Launch independent entity/token files together:
227	Task: "Create VaultEntryMode enum in lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_entry_mode.dart"
228	Task: "Create BiometricCapability enum in lib/features/vault/domain/entities/biometric_capability.dart"
229	Task: "Add sizeKeypadTapTarget token to lib/core/design_tokens.dart"
230	Task: "Create BiometricsPreferenceRepository interface in lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/biometrics_preference_repository.dart"
231	```
232	
233	## Parallel Example: User Story 1 vs. User Story 2 usecases
234	
235	```bash
236	Task: "Create EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase in lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/evaluate_background_resume_usecase.dart"
237	Task: "Write EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase tests in test/features/vault/domain/usecases/evaluate_background_resume_usecase_test.dart"
238	Task: "Create VerifyPinUseCase in lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase.dart"
239	Task: "Write VerifyPinUseCase tests in test/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase_test.dart"
240	```
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Implementation Strategy
245	
246	### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)
247	
248	1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
249	2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks all stories).
250	3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
251	4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: cold launch shows the biometric prompt before data; a successful scan
252	   proceeds; background ≥5 min re-prompts; background <5 min does not. Note that without User
253	   Story 3, this MVP slice has no PIN ever configured on a fresh device — validate it on a device
254	   where a PIN already exists (or treat US1+US3 as the realistic minimum demoable slice).
255	
256	### Incremental Delivery
257	
258	1. Setup + Foundational → foundation ready (vault route exists, resolves to an empty page).
259	2. Add US1 → biometric gate works (needs a pre-existing PIN to reach `unlockBiometricFirst`).
260	3. Add US2 → a failed scan no longer strands the user.
261	4. Add US3 → a fresh device can actually reach the vault for the first time (PIN now gets created) — this closes the loop US1/US2 needed a PIN for.
262	5. Add US4 → the "usar e-mail e senha" safety valve.
263	6. Polish → RNF06/07 gates + quickstart's full manual pass.
264	
265	Note the real dependency the priorities don't show on their own: **US3 produces the PIN that US1
266	and US2 require to exist.** Implementing in spec order (US1 → US2 → US3 → US4) is fine for
267	*writing* the code (Foundational already stubs `hasPinConfigured()`), but *manually demoing* US1/US2
268	end-to-end needs either a PIN seeded directly via `VaultRepository` in a test, or US3 done first.
269	
270	---
271	
272	## Notes
273	
274	- `vault_bloc.dart`, `vault_event.dart`, `vault_state.dart`, and `vault_page.dart` are each touched
275	  by multiple story phases (T021/T027/T036/T043/T044 for the bloc; T022/T028/T037/T045/T048 for the
276	  page) — this is the deliberate single-screen/single-bloc shape research.md R4 chose, not a
277	  same-file conflict to avoid.
278	- Every repository method this unit adds that is *not* network-backed (`VaultRepository`'s methods)
279	  intentionally returns plain types, not `Either<Failure, T>` — research.md R5. Only
280	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save` does, and only its 3 failure-scenario tests (T017) count
281	  toward RNF09's 15/15.
282	- No task in this list touches `docs/input/`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, or
283	  `lib/features/session/presentation/widgets/session_expired_overlay.dart` — all three are
284	  explicitly out of scope (FR-018, spec.md Assumptions).

# Tasks: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. plan.md's Testing section and quickstart.md's "Automated checks" explicitly name
the domain tests this unit's RNF07 coverage gate depends on (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`,
`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`, `VerifyPinUseCase`/`SavePinUseCase`, `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`'s
3 failure scenarios), so test tasks are generated alongside implementation, `bloc_test`/`mocktail`
style, matching F000's existing test files exactly.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (US1–US4, spec.md priorities P1/P1/P2/P3). Per
research.md R4, all four stories share one route/page/bloc (`AppRoutes.vault` / `VaultPage` /
`VaultBloc`) by deliberate design — "independent" here means each story's acceptance scenarios can
be exercised and automated-tested on their own once Foundational is done, not that each story gets
its own screen.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies on an incomplete task)
- **[Story]**: US1 (biometric unlock), US2 (biometric-failure → PIN fallback), US3 (first-time PIN
  setup), US4 (recover via full login)

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (F000's existing `lib/`, `test/`) — see plan.md Project Structure. All new
files live under `lib/features/vault/` and `test/features/vault/`; four files touch existing F000
code at documented one-line extension points.

---

## Phase 1: Setup

**Purpose**: Dependencies and the one new route constant every later task needs.

- [ ] T001 Add `local_auth` and `crypto` to `pubspec.yaml` dependencies (research.md R1, R2), then run `fvm flutter pub get`
- [ ] T002 [P] Add `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` (a one-line usage string) to `ios/Runner/Info.plist` — required before any `local_auth` call, including a check, can be made on-device or in the Simulator (research.md R1)
- [ ] T003 [P] Add `static const String vault = '/vault';` to `AppRoutes` in `lib/core/routing/app_routes.dart`

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: The shared repository/usecase/bloc/page plumbing every one of the four user stories
reads or extends. No story's acceptance scenario can be exercised, manually or in a test, until
this phase is done.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T004 [P] Create `VaultEntryMode` enum (`pinSetupRequired`, `unlockBiometricFirst`, `unlockPinOnly`) in `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/vault_entry_mode.dart` (data-model.md Vault Lock State)
- [ ] T005 [P] Create `BiometricCapability` enum (`available`, `noHardware`, `notEnrolled`, `osDisabled`) in `lib/features/vault/domain/entities/biometric_capability.dart` (data-model.md Biometric Capability)
- [ ] T006 Create `VaultRepository` abstract interface in `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart` — the exact method set from contracts/vault-repository.md (`hasPinConfigured`, `savePin`, `verifyPin`, `checkBiometricCapability`, `attemptBiometricAuth`, `isBiometricPreferenceEnabled`, `setBiometricPreferenceLocally`, `recordBackgrounded`, `consumeBackgroundedAt`, `markUnlocked`, `lastUnlockedAt`), including the `BiometricAuthOutcome` enum (`success`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `notAvailable`) it returns; no `local_auth` or `flutter_secure_storage` type may appear in this file (RNF06) — depends on T004, T005
- [ ] T007 [P] Create `BiometricsPreferenceRepository` abstract interface in `lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/biometrics_preference_repository.dart` — single method `Future<Either<Failure, void>> save(bool enabled)` (contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md)
- [ ] T008 Create `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` in `lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/determine_vault_entry_usecase.dart`, implementing exactly the branching in contracts/vault-repository.md (`!hasPinConfigured()` → `pinSetupRequired`; else `capability == available && preferred` → `unlockBiometricFirst`; else `unlockPinOnly`) — depends on T006
- [ ] T009 [P] Write `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` tests in `test/features/vault/domain/usecases/determine_vault_entry_usecase_test.dart` against a fake `VaultRepository`, covering all four input combinations per quickstart.md: no PIN; PIN + biometric available + preferred; PIN + biometric available + not preferred; PIN + biometric unavailable — depends on T008
- [ ] T010 [P] Add `sizeKeypadTapTarget` token (value `72`, a `double`, dp) to `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` — the circular tap target for each of the keypad's 12 keys, per research.md R7; no other value this unit needs is new
- [ ] T011 Create `VaultSecureStorage` in `lib/features/vault/data/vault_secure_storage.dart` — Keychain-backed via `flutter_secure_storage`, two keys: PIN hash and local biometrics-preference mirror. `savePin`/PIN comparison MUST store and compare only `sha256(pin)` (hex string), never the raw digit string (research.md R2); the PIN value accepted MUST be "exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or compared" (data-model.md Device PIN validation rule) — validate this shape before hashing
- [ ] T012 [P] Create `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` in `lib/features/vault/data/local_auth_biometric_data_source.dart` — thin wrapper over `local_auth`'s `LocalAuthentication`, calling `authenticate(biometricOnly: true)` (research.md R1); the only file in this unit allowed to import `local_auth` types
- [ ] T013 Create `VaultRepositoryImpl` implementing `VaultRepository` in `lib/features/vault/data/vault_repository_impl.dart` — maps `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource`/`local_auth` results into `BiometricCapability`/`BiometricAuthOutcome` before returning (RNF06); `lastUnlockedAt`/`backgroundedAt` held in-memory only, never persisted (data-model.md Vault Lock State) — depends on T006, T011, T012
- [ ] T014 [P] Write `VaultRepositoryImpl` tests in `test/features/vault/data/vault_repository_impl_test.dart` (mocktail, mocking `VaultSecureStorage`/`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource`) covering: PIN hash round-trip (`savePin` then `verifyPin` with the same/different 4-digit value), each `BiometricCapability` mapping, `recordBackgrounded`/`consumeBackgroundedAt` clearing semantics (one resume evaluates the gap only once), `markUnlocked`/`lastUnlockedAt` — depends on T013
- [ ] T015 Create `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` in `lib/features/vault/data/account/biometrics_preference_remote_data_source.dart` — `update({required bool biometricEnabled})` calling `ApiClient.call('account-settings-update', method: 'PATCH', body: {'biometricEnabled': biometricEnabled})` exactly as in contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md
- [ ] T016 Create `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl` implementing `BiometricsPreferenceRepository` in `lib/features/vault/data/account/biometrics_preference_repository_impl.dart` — `save(enabled)` delegates to the remote data source and maps `Right` to `Right(unit)` via `.map((_) {})`, discarding the decoded body (contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md: "there is no reason to decode and carry the full updated-account payload") — depends on T007, T015
- [ ] T017 [P] Write `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl` tests in `test/features/vault/data/account/biometrics_preference_repository_impl_test.dart` (mocktail, mocking `ApiClient`, matching `auth_repository_impl_test.dart`'s pattern) covering the 4 scenarios from contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md: `Right({...})` → `Right(unit)`; `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure)` passes through unchanged; `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` passes through unchanged; `Left(ValidationFailure)` (malformed response) passes through unchanged — depends on T016
- [ ] T018 Register this unit's dependencies in `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`: `VaultSecureStorage`, `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource`, `VaultRepository` as `registerLazySingleton` (one instance for the app's process lifetime, per contracts/vault-repository.md), `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource`, `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`, `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`, and `VaultBloc` as `registerFactory` (matching `AuthBloc`'s registration shape) — depends on T006, T007, T008, T013, T016
- [ ] T019 Create `VaultState` in `lib/features/vault/presentation/bloc/vault_state.dart` — sub-states covering every branch this unit's single bloc must represent: initial/loading, PIN setup (create step, confirm step with mismatch error), biometric prompting, PIN entry (with the optional "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" error banner and a 4-digit progress-dot count), unlocked

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies — start immediately.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup (T003 for the route constant) — BLOCKS all user stories.
- **User Stories (Phase 3–6)**: All depend on Foundational completion.
  - US1 and US2 (both P1) should be done first — US2's "biometric fails → PIN" handler extends the
    same `VaultBloc` branch US1's biometric-success handler lives in (T027/T036 both touch
    `vault_bloc.dart`), so doing them in sequence avoids rework, even though each is independently
    testable once done.
  - US3 (P2) extends the same bloc/page with the `pinSetupRequired` branch — independent of US1/US2's
    code paths (different `VaultEntryMode` branch) but shares the file.
  - US4 (P3) only adds a link + navigation handler on top of UI states US1/US2 already built (T028, T037).
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: Depends on all four stories being complete.

### Within Each User Story

- Tests before/alongside implementation (written to fail first, per the template's convention).
- Domain usecases before bloc wiring; bloc wiring before the page UI that reads it.
- Story complete (bloc + page + test) before moving to the next priority.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T002, T003 (Setup) in parallel.
- T004, T005 (entities), T010 (design token), T007 (second repository interface) in parallel within Foundational.
- T009, T014, T017 (test files) can be written in parallel with each other once their respective implementation task lands.
- T025/T026 (US1 usecase + its test) in parallel with T034/T035 (US2 usecase + its test) — different files, both depend only on Foundational.
- T039/T040/T041 (US3 usecases + tests) in parallel with each other.

Task: "Create BiometricCapability enum in lib/features/vault/domain/entities/biometric_capability.dart"
Task: "Add sizeKeypadTapTarget token to lib/core/design_tokens.dart"

## Parallel Example: User Story 1 vs. User Story 2 usecases

```bash

Task: "Write EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase tests in test/features/vault/domain/usecases/evaluate_background_resume_usecase_test.dart"
Task: "Create VerifyPinUseCase in lib/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase.dart"
Task: "Write VerifyPinUseCase tests in test/features/vault/domain/usecases/verify_pin_usecase_test.dart"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup.
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL — blocks all stories).
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1.
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: cold launch shows the biometric prompt before data; a successful scan
   proceeds; background ≥5 min re-prompts; background <5 min does not. Note that without User
   Story 3, this MVP slice has no PIN ever configured on a fresh device — validate it on a device
   where a PIN already exists (or treat US1+US3 as the realistic minimum demoable slice).

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → foundation ready (vault route exists, resolves to an empty page).
2. Add US1 → biometric gate works (needs a pre-existing PIN to reach `unlockBiometricFirst`).
3. Add US2 → a failed scan no longer strands the user.
4. Add US3 → a fresh device can actually reach the vault for the first time (PIN now gets created) — this closes the loop US1/US2 needed a PIN for.
5. Add US4 → the "usar e-mail e senha" safety valve.
6. Polish → RNF06/07 gates + quickstart's full manual pass.

Note the real dependency the priorities don't show on their own: **US3 produces the PIN that US1
and US2 require to exist.** Implementing in spec order (US1 → US2 → US3 → US4) is fine for
*writing* the code (Foundational already stubs `hasPinConfigured()`), but *manually demoing* US1/US2
end-to-end needs either a PIN seeded directly via `VaultRepository` in a test, or US3 done first.

## Notes

- `vault_bloc.dart`, `vault_event.dart`, `vault_state.dart`, and `vault_page.dart` are each touched
  by multiple story phases (T021/T027/T036/T043/T044 for the bloc; T022/T028/T037/T045/T048 for the
  page) — this is the deliberate single-screen/single-bloc shape research.md R4 chose, not a
  same-file conflict to avoid.
- Every repository method this unit adds that is *not* network-backed (`VaultRepository`'s methods)
  intentionally returns plain types, not `Either<Failure, T>` — research.md R5. Only
  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save` does, and only its 3 failure-scenario tests (T017) count
  toward RNF09's 15/15.
- No task in this list touches `docs/input/`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, or
  `lib/features/session/presentation/widgets/session_expired_overlay.dart` — all three are
  explicitly out of scope (FR-018, spec.md Assumptions).

1	# Data Model: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1, 6.1, 10, prototype-extract.md §§2.1, 3.
4	Entities here are either on-device-only domain objects (Device PIN, Vault Lock State) or a local
5	mirror of one backend field (Biometrics Preference) — this unit introduces no new backend table
6	and no new local database (just two new secure-storage keys alongside F000's four).
7	
8	## Device PIN
9	
10	A 4-digit secret, created once (User Story 3) and checked on every subsequent unlock attempt
11	(User Stories 1–2). Never transmitted to, or validated by, the backend (FR-002).
12	
13	| Field | Type | Notes |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| `pinHash` | `String` (hex, sha256) | Written by `VaultSecureStorage`; see research.md R2 for why the raw digit string is never the thing stored. |
16	
17	**Validation rule**: exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or
18	compared (FR-005). Confirmation during setup is a pure string-equality check between two freshly
19	entered 4-digit values — the first one is held only in memory (`VaultState`) between entry and
20	confirmation, never written to storage until it matches (FR-012: "without the mismatched PIN being
21	saved").
22	
23	## Vault Lock State
24	
25	Whether the current app process currently requires authentication before showing data, and when it
26	was last satisfied — the input to the 5-minute background-resume rule (FR-007–FR-010).
27	
28	| Field | Type | Notes |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| `lastUnlockedAt` | `DateTime?` | In-memory only, held by the `VaultRepository` singleton (one instance for the app's lifetime via `get_it`'s `registerLazySingleton`). `null` until the first successful unlock this process. Never persisted to disk — see research.md R3 for why a killed/relaunched process doesn't need this to survive. |
31	| `backgroundedAt` | `DateTime?` | Set by `VaultLifecycleObserver` on `AppLifecycleState.paused`; read and cleared on the matching `.resumed`. In-memory only, same lifetime as `lastUnlockedAt`. |
32	
33	**Derived decision — `VaultEntryMode`** (domain enum/sealed type, computed by
34	`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` every time `VaultPage` opens):
35	
36	```
37	pinSetupRequired                      # hasPinConfigured() == false
38	unlockBiometricFirst                  # PIN exists AND biometric capability == available
39	                                       #   AND the local biometrics-preference mirror == true
40	unlockPinOnly                         # PIN exists AND (no biometric capability OR preference == false)
41	```
42	
43	**State transitions**:
44	
45	```
46	[SplashPage, SessionStatusAuthenticated]  or  [LoginSignupPage, AuthStatus.authenticated (non-reauth)]
47	  context.push(AppRoutes.vault)   # mode: gatekeeper
48	      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()
49	          pinSetupRequired      -> show "Digite seu PIN" (new) -> confirm -> [optional] offer biometrics
50	                                     -> on complete: context.go(AppRoutes.home)     (Story 3)
51	          unlockBiometricFirst  -> auto-trigger local_auth prompt
52	              success            -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)   (Story 1)
53	              failed/cancelled   -> show "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" + PIN keypad (Story 2)
54	                  correct PIN      -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)
55	                  incorrect PIN    -> clear digits, keep error banner, no lockout, retry allowed (Story 2, Edge Cases)
56	          unlockPinOnly          -> show PIN keypad directly, no biometric prompt attempted (Edge Cases: no hardware/not enrolled/OS-disabled)
57	      at any point: "usar e-mail e senha" -> context.push(AppRoutes.login)          (Story 4)
58	
59	[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == true]
60	  rootNavigatorKey.push(VaultPage)   # mode: relock — pushed OVER whatever screen is current
61	      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()   # always unlockBiometricFirst or unlockPinOnly — PIN already exists
62	          success (biometric or PIN)  -> markUnlocked() -> Navigator.pop()   # reveals the preserved screen underneath, state untouched
63	
64	[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == false]
65	  no-op — screen underneath was never covered, no re-authentication required   (FR-008)
66	```
67	
68	**Fixed rule** (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`, FR-009):
69	
70	```dart
71	bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
72	  if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
73	  return resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= const Duration(minutes: 5);
74	}
75	```
76	
77	A pure function of two timestamps and one constant — no settings read, no parameter — is itself
78	the mechanism by which FR-009's "fixed value, not configurable by the user" is enforced.
79	
80	## Biometrics Preference
81	
82	An account-level flag indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's chosen unlock method —
83	read locally at every vault entry to decide `unlockBiometricFirst` vs. `unlockPinOnly`, and mirrored
84	to the backend for durability/future display (RF09's Settings screen), per FR-013.
85	
86	| Field | Type | Notes |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| `biometricPreferenceLocal` | `bool` | Written to `VaultSecureStorage` during first-time PIN setup (Story 3, scenario 4) if the user opts in; this is the value `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads at runtime — never the backend's copy (research.md R6). Defaults to `false` until set. |
89	| `biometricEnabled` (remote) | `bool` | The backend's `users.biometric_enabled` field (requirements.md §8), read/written only through `PATCH /account/settings` → `account-settings-update`. This unit only ever **writes** it (fire-and-forget, FR-014); it never reads it back. |
90	
91	**Write path** (`SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, FR-013/FR-014):
92	
93	```
94	1. VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)        # synchronous, always succeeds (local write)
95	2. BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)                  # await, discard Either<Failure, T> result
96	3. proceed to Home/Chat regardless of step 2's outcome            # Clarifications; Edge Cases
97	```
98	
99	## Backend Failure (reused, not redefined)
100	
101	`BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` is the only network call this unit makes; it returns
102	`Either<Failure, T>` using F000's existing `core/network/failure.dart` hierarchy unchanged (no new
103	`Failure` subtype — research.md R5). The three scenarios covered by this unit's own tests, toward
104	RNF09's 15-scenario total:
105	
106	| Scenario | Expected `Failure` | `retryable` |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| Request exceeds the timeout | `NetworkTimeoutFailure` | yes |
109	| No connection at all | `NetworkOfflineFailure` | yes |
110	| Malformed response body | `ValidationFailure` | no |
111	
112	None of these three block the PIN-setup-complete transition (R6) — they are observed only by this
113	unit's own `mocktail` tests of `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`, never surfaced to the user.
114	
115	## Biometric Capability (domain enum, no `local_auth` type crosses into `domain/`)
116	
117	```
118	available        # canCheckBiometrics && isDeviceSupported && getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty
119	noHardware        # isDeviceSupported == false
120	notEnrolled        # hardware present, nothing enrolled at the OS level
121	osDisabled        # was available in a previous session, no longer (Edge Cases: OS-level disable between sessions)
122	```
