# Data Model: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1, 6.1, 10, prototype-extract.md §§2.1, 3.
Entities here are either on-device-only domain objects (Device PIN, Vault Lock State) or a local
mirror of one backend field (Biometrics Preference) — this unit introduces no new backend table
and no new local database (just two new secure-storage keys alongside F000's four).

## Device PIN

A 4-digit secret, created once (User Story 3) and checked on every subsequent unlock attempt
(User Stories 1–2). Never transmitted to, or validated by, the backend (FR-002).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pinHash` | `String` (hex, sha256) | Written by `VaultSecureStorage`; see research.md R2 for why the raw digit string is never the thing stored. |

**Validation rule**: exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or
compared (FR-005). Confirmation during setup is a pure string-equality check between two freshly
entered 4-digit values — the first one is held only in memory (`VaultState`) between entry and
confirmation, never written to storage until it matches (FR-012: "without the mismatched PIN being
saved").

## Vault Lock State

Whether the current app process currently requires authentication before showing data, and when it
was last satisfied — the input to the 5-minute background-resume rule (FR-007–FR-010).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `lastUnlockedAt` | `DateTime?` | In-memory only, held by the `VaultRepository` singleton (one instance for the app's lifetime via `get_it`'s `registerLazySingleton`). `null` until the first successful unlock this process. Never persisted to disk — see research.md R3 for why a killed/relaunched process doesn't need this to survive. |
| `backgroundedAt` | `DateTime?` | Set by `VaultLifecycleObserver` on `AppLifecycleState.paused`; read and cleared on the matching `.resumed`. In-memory only, same lifetime as `lastUnlockedAt`. |

**Derived decision — `VaultEntryMode`** (domain enum/sealed type, computed by
`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` every time `VaultPage` opens):

```
pinSetupRequired                      # hasPinConfigured() == false
unlockBiometricFirst                  # PIN exists AND biometric capability == available
                                       #   AND the local biometrics-preference mirror == true
unlockPinOnly                         # PIN exists AND (no biometric capability OR preference == false)
```

**State transitions**:

```
[SplashPage, SessionStatusAuthenticated]  or  [LoginSignupPage, AuthStatus.authenticated (non-reauth)]
  context.push(AppRoutes.vault)   # mode: gatekeeper
      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()
          pinSetupRequired      -> show "Digite seu PIN" (new) -> confirm -> [optional] offer biometrics
                                     -> on complete: context.go(AppRoutes.home)     (Story 3)
          unlockBiometricFirst  -> auto-trigger local_auth prompt
              success            -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)   (Story 1)
              failed/cancelled   -> show "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" + PIN keypad (Story 2)
                  correct PIN      -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)
                  incorrect PIN    -> clear digits, keep error banner, no lockout, retry allowed (Story 2, Edge Cases)
          unlockPinOnly          -> show PIN keypad directly, no biometric prompt attempted (Edge Cases: no hardware/not enrolled/OS-disabled)
      at any point: "usar e-mail e senha" -> context.push(AppRoutes.login)          (Story 4)

[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == true]
  rootNavigatorKey.push(VaultPage)   # mode: relock — pushed OVER whatever screen is current
      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()   # always unlockBiometricFirst or unlockPinOnly — PIN already exists
          success (biometric or PIN)  -> markUnlocked() -> Navigator.pop()   # reveals the preserved screen underneath, state untouched

[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == false]
  no-op — screen underneath was never covered, no re-authentication required   (FR-008)
```

**Fixed rule** (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`, FR-009):

```dart
bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
  if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
  return resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= const Duration(minutes: 5);
}
```

A pure function of two timestamps and one constant — no settings read, no parameter — is itself
the mechanism by which FR-009's "fixed value, not configurable by the user" is enforced.

## Biometrics Preference

An account-level flag indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's chosen unlock method —
read locally at every vault entry to decide `unlockBiometricFirst` vs. `unlockPinOnly`, and mirrored
to the backend for durability/future display (RF09's Settings screen), per FR-013.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `biometricPreferenceLocal` | `bool` | Written to `VaultSecureStorage` during first-time PIN setup (Story 3, scenario 4) if the user opts in; this is the value `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads at runtime — never the backend's copy (research.md R6). Defaults to `false` until set. |
| `biometricEnabled` (remote) | `bool` | The backend's `users.biometric_enabled` field (requirements.md §8), read/written only through `PATCH /account/settings` → `account-settings-update`. This unit only ever **writes** it (fire-and-forget, FR-014); it never reads it back. |

**Write path** (`SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, FR-013/FR-014):

```
1. VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)        # synchronous, always succeeds (local write)
2. BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)                  # await, discard Either<Failure, T> result
3. proceed to Home/Chat regardless of step 2's outcome            # Clarifications; Edge Cases
```

## Backend Failure (reused, not redefined)

`BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` is the only network call this unit makes; it returns
`Either<Failure, T>` using F000's existing `core/network/failure.dart` hierarchy unchanged (no new
`Failure` subtype — research.md R5). The three scenarios covered by this unit's own tests, toward
RNF09's 15-scenario total:

| Scenario | Expected `Failure` | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| Request exceeds the timeout | `NetworkTimeoutFailure` | yes |
| No connection at all | `NetworkOfflineFailure` | yes |
| Malformed response body | `ValidationFailure` | no |

None of these three block the PIN-setup-complete transition (R6) — they are observed only by this
unit's own `mocktail` tests of `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`, never surfaced to the user.

## Biometric Capability (domain enum, no `local_auth` type crosses into `domain/`)

```
available        # canCheckBiometrics && isDeviceSupported && getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty
noHardware        # isDeviceSupported == false
notEnrolled        # hardware present, nothing enrolled at the OS level
osDisabled        # was available in a previous session, no longer (Edge Cases: OS-level disable between sessions)
```

`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` (data layer) is the only place that imports `local_auth`'s own
types (`LocalAuthentication`, `AuthenticationOptions`, `BiometricType`); `VaultRepositoryImpl` maps
its result into this enum before it ever reaches `domain/` or `presentation/` (RNF06).

## Presentation-only state (not persisted, not a domain entity)

- **`VaultMode`** (`gatekeeper | relock`) — which of the two entry points opened `VaultPage`;
  decides `go(home)` vs. `pop()` on success (data-model.md State transitions above). Passed as a
  constructor parameter, not stored anywhere.
- **First-entry PIN held during confirmation** — the first 4-digit value typed during first-time
  setup, kept only in `VaultBloc`'s in-memory state until the confirmation entry either matches
  (written to storage) or doesn't (discarded, user restarts entry — FR-012).
- **PIN-entry digit buffer / progress-dot count** — transient widget/bloc state for the keypad,
  reset to empty after every failed attempt (Edge Cases: "the entered digits are cleared").

## Design Tokens (`lib/core/design_tokens.dart`) — additions only

Every color, type style, spacing, and radius the vault screens use already exists from F000
(`colorPrimary`, `colorOnPrimary`, `colorError`, `colorSurfaceBg`, `textHeadlineMd`, `textBodyMd`,
`textTitleSm`, `spacing*`, `radius*`). One value is new, per research.md R7:

| Token | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `sizeKeypadTapTarget` | `72` (double, dp) | `pin_keypad.dart` — the circular tap target for each of the 12 keys (digits 0–9 + backspace + the empty 4th-row-left cell), per the prototype's "3×4 numeric keypad" with no explicit pixel size given. |

No other component-level token (spine colors, sync badge, bookmark states, etc.) is needed — those
belong to later units' own screens, same precedent F000's data-model.md already set.

1	# Research: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	F000's research.md explicitly left "biometrics" open for "the units that need them (RF03, RF09)."
4	This file resolves that, plus every other free choice and silent spot this unit's spec surfaces.
5	
6	## R1 — Biometrics package
7	
8	- **Decision**: `local_auth` (the official `flutter.dev`-maintained plugin), called with
9	  `authenticate(biometricOnly: true)`.
10	- **Rationale**: FR-004 requires that a failed/unavailable biometric attempt fall through to the
11	  app's **own** 4-digit PIN, never to the iOS device passcode. `local_auth`'s `biometricOnly: true`
12	  option is honored on iOS (it pins the underlying `LAPolicy` to
13	  `LAPolicyDeviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics`, which has no device-passcode fallback built
14	  in) — exactly the primitive FR-004 needs. `local_auth` also exposes `canCheckBiometrics` and
15	  `isDeviceSupported()` ahead of calling `authenticate`, which FR-003 and the Edge Cases ("no
16	  hardware," "nothing enrolled," "disabled at the OS level") need to distinguish from an in-progress
17	  failed attempt. It is the only Flutter-ecosystem plugin maintained by the Flutter team itself for
18	  this exact purpose, consistent with picking boring, well-supported dependencies for a stack the
19	  constitution otherwise keeps deliberately small.
20	- **Alternatives considered**: Rolling a native iOS `LAContext` call through a hand-written
21	  platform channel — rejected, `local_auth` already wraps exactly this with no extra capability
22	  gained from going lower-level, for meaningfully more code to own and test. Third-party biometrics
23	  wrappers (e.g. ones that bundle PIN-entry UI too) — rejected, this unit already owns PIN entry per
24	  FR-005/the prototype's exact keypad spec, and a bundled UI would fight Principle IV (design-token
25	  fidelity) rather than help.
26	- **Native project note**: `local_auth`'s iOS backend requires `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` in
27	  `ios/Runner/Info.plist` (a one-line string the App Store requires before Face ID can even be
28	  attempted) — the only native project file this unit touches, and a hard requirement of the
29	  package rather than a product decision. No Android work exists in this project (iOS-only,
30	  Principle II).
31	
32	## R2 — PIN storage
33	
34	- **Decision**: Store `sha256(pin)` (hex string) via a new `VaultSecureStorage` key, never the raw
35	  4-digit value. Verification re-hashes the entered PIN and compares digests.
36	- **Rationale**: `flutter_secure_storage` is already Keychain-backed (R5 of F000's research.md),
37	  so storing the raw PIN would not be *readable* in plaintext at rest either — but hashing is the
38	  standard defense-in-depth for any credential-shaped value regardless of the storage layer
39	  underneath, and it is a one-function addition (`crypto`'s `sha256`) with no behavioral
40	  downside: the PIN is never displayed back to the user, so there is no legitimate need to ever
41	  recover the raw value, only to compare it. This mirrors how the backend itself never stores or
42	  sees passwords in the clear.
43	- **Alternatives considered**: Storing the raw PIN string — rejected as an avoidable weakening for
44	  zero functional gain. A salted hash (per-install random salt, also stored) — rejected as
45	  over-engineering: the threat a salt defends against is an attacker who has compromised *many*
46	  users' hash stores at once and wants to precompute one rainbow table across all of them; here,
47	  each hash lives alone inside that one device's own encrypted Keychain entry for that one user, so
48	  a salt adds code and a second stored value without changing what an attacker who already has
49	  Keychain access could do.
50	
51	## R3 — Where the 5-minute relock timer lives
52	
53	- **Decision**: One root-level `StatefulWidget` (`VaultLifecycleObserver`), installed once in
54	  `main.dart`'s `CerneApp.builder` (the same spot F000 installs the session-expired
55	  `BlocListener`), implementing `WidgetsBindingObserver`. On `AppLifecycleState.paused` it calls
56	  into the long-lived `VaultRepository` singleton to record "now"; on `.resumed` it asks a pure
57	  domain usecase (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`) whether that gap was ≥ 5 minutes, and if so
58	  pushes `VaultPage(mode: relock)` via the existing `rootNavigatorKey` — the same root navigator
59	  `session_expired_overlay.dart` already pushes onto.
60	- **Rationale**: FR-007/FR-008/FR-010 and User Story 1's background-resume scenarios are a
61	  cross-cutting concern that has nothing to do with *which* screen happens to be on top — exactly
62	  the shape F000's own `SessionBloc` + root `BlocListener` pattern was built for (research.md R3
63	  there). Reusing `rootNavigatorKey` and plain `push` (never `go`/replace) is what makes "the screen
64	  underneath keeps its exact state" (FR-010) true by construction, not by a second bespoke
65	  mechanism — the same guarantee `session_expired_overlay.dart` already relies on for its own
66	  overlay.
67	- **Why not persist the last-unlock timestamp to disk**: the only case that would matter for is the
68	  OS killing the process while backgrounded — but that case is *already* handled for free: a killed
69	  process means the next launch is a cold launch, which always re-enters `SplashPage` → the
70	  `AppRoutes.vault` gatekeeper path regardless of elapsed time (Edge Cases: "the next launch is
71	  treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault"). An in-memory timestamp on a singleton
72	  repository is therefore sufficient; persisting it would add a disk write on every background
73	  transition for a case that can't be reached.
74	- **Alternatives considered**: A second root-level `Bloc` dedicated to lock state — rejected as an
75	  unnecessary extra moving part; the logic needed (record a timestamp, compare it, decide whether
76	  to push one specific, already-existing route) does not need its own event/state machine distinct
77	  from the domain usecase plus a thin observer widget. A `Timer.periodic` ticking down from 5
78	  minutes while foregrounded — rejected: FR-007/FR-008 only care about elapsed *background* time,
79	  not foreground idle time (that is RF08's unrelated 2-minute inactivity trigger), so a running
80	  foreground timer would be solving a problem this requirement doesn't have.
81	
82	## R4 — The single-screen vault (gatekeeper vs. relock, setup vs. unlock)
83	
84	- **Decision**: One route (`AppRoutes.vault`), one page (`VaultPage`), one screen-scoped
85	  `VaultBloc`, branching internally on two independent axes: (a) **mode** — `gatekeeper` (reached
86	  from `SplashPage` or `LoginSignupPage`, resolves by going to `AppRoutes.home` on success) vs.
87	  `relock` (reached from `VaultLifecycleObserver`, resolves by popping back to the preserved screen
88	  underneath); (b) **entry decision** — `pinSetupRequired` vs. `locked(biometricFirst | pinOnly)`,
89	  computed once by `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` when the page opens.
90	- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md's own implementation note #1 flags that "32 states" collapse
91	  into fewer real screens with internal state, naming this exact family (Biometria / PIN inicial /
92	  PIN após falha) as a candidate. The spec's own Assumptions go further and fold first-time PIN
93	  creation into the same keypad component rather than inventing a fourth undocumented screen. A
94	  `relock` entry can never need the `pinSetupRequired` branch (a relock is only ever triggered after
95	  the app was already unlocked once this process, which requires a PIN to already exist) — so the
96	  same `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` naturally degrades to just the unlock branch for that mode
97	  without needing a second decision function.
98	- **Alternatives considered**: Four separate routes (one per prototype state name) — rejected,
99	  directly contradicts the prototype's own implementation note and would duplicate the keypad
100	  widget and its 350 ms-after-4th-digit transition behavior four times instead of once.
101	
102	## R5 — RNF09 scoping for this unit's local-only operations
103	
104	- **Decision**: `Either<Failure, T>` is used only where this unit actually talks to the network —
105	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`. `VaultRepository` (PIN verification, biometric hardware
106	  queries, the in-memory relock timestamp) returns plain `bool`/`DateTime?`/domain-enum values, not
107	  `Either<Failure, T>`.
108	- **Rationale**: RNF09's `Failure` hierarchy (`core/network/failure.dart`) is explicitly the
109	  backend's own closed 13-code taxonomy (F000 research.md R6) — `AUTH_EXPIRED`,
110	  `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, and so on are all things *a server response* can say. A missing fingerprint
111	  sensor or a wrong PIN digest is not a server outcome and has no corresponding code; forcing it
112	  through `Either<Failure, T>` would mean either inventing fake codes for purely local conditions
113	  (polluting a taxonomy the spec calls "closed") or always returning a code that doesn't really fit.
114	  Constitution Principle I directs implementers to make the reasonable call where the inputs are
115	  silent, and RNF09's own wording ("every repository") is about the network-error-handling pattern
116	  the requirement is named for — not a blanket ban on any repository ever returning something else
117	  for a condition that isn't a network failure.
118	- **Alternatives considered**: Modeling PIN/biometric outcomes as `Either<Failure, T>` with new
119	  `Failure` subtypes (e.g. `BiometricUnavailableFailure`) — rejected: it would grow the "closed"
120	  taxonomy with codes the backend's `error-taxonomy.md` doesn't define and that no later unit's
121	  network code would ever need to pattern-match on, diluting the one place (`failure.dart`) F000
122	  deliberately kept scoped to the backend's own 13 codes (F000 research.md R6).
123	
124	## R6 — `biometricEnabled` write semantics (building on the Clarifications session)
125	
126	- **Decision**: `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` writes the local mirror flag
127	  (`VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally`) synchronously, then fires the
128	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` network call and discards its `Either` result — no retry
129	  loop, no error banner, no blocking of the PIN-setup-complete transition to Home/Chat.
130	- **Rationale**: This is the literal mechanics of the Clarifications session's resolution
131	  ("proceed locally and retry in the background... first-time setup does not block on this write
132	  succeeding") plus the matching Edge Case ("the write is not retried synchronously as part of the
133	  setup flow"). The *local* mirror is what every later vault unlock actually reads to decide
134	  biometric-first vs. PIN-only (FR-003) — the backend's copy of `biometricEnabled` is a durable
135	  record for whichever later unit (RF09's Settings screen) needs to display or change it, not the
136	  value this unit's own unlock logic depends on at runtime.
137	- **What "retry through the existing failure-handling path" means here**: concretely, nothing new
138	  is built for it in this unit — the failed write simply isn't retried by RF03 at all. If the user
139	  later opens Settings (RF09) and that screen reads the account record, any mismatch between the
140	  local mirror and the stale backend value is that unit's reconciliation problem, not this one's;
141	  RF03 does not introduce a background sync queue, which would be speculative machinery for a case
142	  the spec explicitly says not to block on.
143	- **Alternatives considered**: A `WorkManager`/background-retry-queue style mechanism — rejected as
144	  out of proportion to a single boolean field and explicitly not what the Clarifications answer
145	  asked for.
146	
147	## R7 — New design tokens this unit needs
148	
149	- **Decision**: Add exactly one new token, `sizeKeypadTapTarget` (72 dp — a 4×-grid value,
150	  consistent with the existing `spacing*` scale, sized for a comfortable thumb target per the
151	  prototype's 390×844 frame), to `design_tokens.dart`. Everything else the vault screens need
152	  (error-band red, primary buttons, body/title text styles, spacing, radii) already exists from
153	  F000.
154	- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md §3 does not give the PIN keypad an explicit pixel size (only
155	  "3×4 numeric keypad with backspace"), so this is the one silent spot Principle I's "reasonable
156	  technical decision" applies to visually — and per Principle IV it must still be a named constant
157	  in `design_tokens.dart`, not an inline literal in `pin_keypad.dart`.
158	- **Icons**: continuing F000's already-established precedent of using Flutter's built-in
159	  `Icons.*` (Material) rather than the prototype's specified Phosphor set (F000 used `Icons.send`,
160	  `Icons.lock` — see `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `session_expired_overlay.dart`) — this unit uses
161	  `Icons.fingerprint` (Biometria's fingerprint circle), `Icons.backspace` (keypad backspace), and
162	  `Icons.lock_outline` (PIN screen header), introducing no new icon package.

- **Rationale**: FR-007/FR-008/FR-010 and User Story 1's background-resume scenarios are a
  cross-cutting concern that has nothing to do with *which* screen happens to be on top — exactly
  the shape F000's own `SessionBloc` + root `BlocListener` pattern was built for (research.md R3
  there). Reusing `rootNavigatorKey` and plain `push` (never `go`/replace) is what makes "the screen
  underneath keeps its exact state" (FR-010) true by construction, not by a second bespoke
  mechanism — the same guarantee `session_expired_overlay.dart` already relies on for its own
  overlay.
- **Why not persist the last-unlock timestamp to disk**: the only case that would matter for is the
  OS killing the process while backgrounded — but that case is *already* handled for free: a killed
  process means the next launch is a cold launch, which always re-enters `SplashPage` → the
  `AppRoutes.vault` gatekeeper path regardless of elapsed time (Edge Cases: "the next launch is
  treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault"). An in-memory timestamp on a singleton
  repository is therefore sufficient; persisting it would add a disk write on every background
  transition for a case that can't be reached.
- **Alternatives considered**: A second root-level `Bloc` dedicated to lock state — rejected as an
  unnecessary extra moving part; the logic needed (record a timestamp, compare it, decide whether
  to push one specific, already-existing route) does not need its own event/state machine distinct
  from the domain usecase plus a thin observer widget. A `Timer.periodic` ticking down from 5
  minutes while foregrounded — rejected: FR-007/FR-008 only care about elapsed *background* time,
  not foreground idle time (that is RF08's unrelated 2-minute inactivity trigger), so a running
  foreground timer would be solving a problem this requirement doesn't have.

## R4 — The single-screen vault (gatekeeper vs. relock, setup vs. unlock)

- **Decision**: One route (`AppRoutes.vault`), one page (`VaultPage`), one screen-scoped
  `VaultBloc`, branching internally on two independent axes: (a) **mode** — `gatekeeper` (reached
  from `SplashPage` or `LoginSignupPage`, resolves by going to `AppRoutes.home` on success) vs.
  `relock` (reached from `VaultLifecycleObserver`, resolves by popping back to the preserved screen
  underneath); (b) **entry decision** — `pinSetupRequired` vs. `locked(biometricFirst | pinOnly)`,
  computed once by `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` when the page opens.
- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md's own implementation note #1 flags that "32 states" collapse
  into fewer real screens with internal state, naming this exact family (Biometria / PIN inicial /
  PIN após falha) as a candidate. The spec's own Assumptions go further and fold first-time PIN
  creation into the same keypad component rather than inventing a fourth undocumented screen. A
  `relock` entry can never need the `pinSetupRequired` branch (a relock is only ever triggered after
  the app was already unlocked once this process, which requires a PIN to already exist) — so the
  same `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` naturally degrades to just the unlock branch for that mode
  without needing a second decision function.
- **Alternatives considered**: Four separate routes (one per prototype state name) — rejected,
  directly contradicts the prototype's own implementation note and would duplicate the keypad
  widget and its 350 ms-after-4th-digit transition behavior four times instead of once.

## R5 — RNF09 scoping for this unit's local-only operations

- **Decision**: `Either<Failure, T>` is used only where this unit actually talks to the network —
  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`. `VaultRepository` (PIN verification, biometric hardware
  queries, the in-memory relock timestamp) returns plain `bool`/`DateTime?`/domain-enum values, not
  `Either<Failure, T>`.
- **Rationale**: RNF09's `Failure` hierarchy (`core/network/failure.dart`) is explicitly the
  backend's own closed 13-code taxonomy (F000 research.md R6) — `AUTH_EXPIRED`,
  `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, and so on are all things *a server response* can say. A missing fingerprint
  sensor or a wrong PIN digest is not a server outcome and has no corresponding code; forcing it
  through `Either<Failure, T>` would mean either inventing fake codes for purely local conditions
  (polluting a taxonomy the spec calls "closed") or always returning a code that doesn't really fit.
  Constitution Principle I directs implementers to make the reasonable call where the inputs are
  silent, and RNF09's own wording ("every repository") is about the network-error-handling pattern
  the requirement is named for — not a blanket ban on any repository ever returning something else
  for a condition that isn't a network failure.
- **Alternatives considered**: Modeling PIN/biometric outcomes as `Either<Failure, T>` with new
  `Failure` subtypes (e.g. `BiometricUnavailableFailure`) — rejected: it would grow the "closed"
  taxonomy with codes the backend's `error-taxonomy.md` doesn't define and that no later unit's
  network code would ever need to pattern-match on, diluting the one place (`failure.dart`) F000
  deliberately kept scoped to the backend's own 13 codes (F000 research.md R6).

## R6 — `biometricEnabled` write semantics (building on the Clarifications session)

- **Decision**: `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` writes the local mirror flag
  (`VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally`) synchronously, then fires the
  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` network call and discards its `Either` result — no retry
  loop, no error banner, no blocking of the PIN-setup-complete transition to Home/Chat.
- **Rationale**: This is the literal mechanics of the Clarifications session's resolution
  ("proceed locally and retry in the background... first-time setup does not block on this write
  succeeding") plus the matching Edge Case ("the write is not retried synchronously as part of the
  setup flow"). The *local* mirror is what every later vault unlock actually reads to decide
  biometric-first vs. PIN-only (FR-003) — the backend's copy of `biometricEnabled` is a durable
  record for whichever later unit (RF09's Settings screen) needs to display or change it, not the
  value this unit's own unlock logic depends on at runtime.
- **What "retry through the existing failure-handling path" means here**: concretely, nothing new
  is built for it in this unit — the failed write simply isn't retried by RF03 at all. If the user
  later opens Settings (RF09) and that screen reads the account record, any mismatch between the
  local mirror and the stale backend value is that unit's reconciliation problem, not this one's;
  RF03 does not introduce a background sync queue, which would be speculative machinery for a case
  the spec explicitly says not to block on.
- **Alternatives considered**: A `WorkManager`/background-retry-queue style mechanism — rejected as
  out of proportion to a single boolean field and explicitly not what the Clarifications answer
  asked for.

## R7 — New design tokens this unit needs

- **Decision**: Add exactly one new token, `sizeKeypadTapTarget` (72 dp — a 4×-grid value,
  consistent with the existing `spacing*` scale, sized for a comfortable thumb target per the
  prototype's 390×844 frame), to `design_tokens.dart`. Everything else the vault screens need
  (error-band red, primary buttons, body/title text styles, spacing, radii) already exists from
  F000.
- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md §3 does not give the PIN keypad an explicit pixel size (only
  "3×4 numeric keypad with backspace"), so this is the one silent spot Principle I's "reasonable
  technical decision" applies to visually — and per Principle IV it must still be a named constant
  in `design_tokens.dart`, not an inline literal in `pin_keypad.dart`.
- **Icons**: continuing F000's already-established precedent of using Flutter's built-in
  `Icons.*` (Material) rather than the prototype's specified Phosphor set (F000 used `Icons.send`,
  `Icons.lock` — see `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `session_expired_overlay.dart`) — this unit uses
  `Icons.fingerprint` (Biometria's fingerprint circle), `Icons.backspace` (keypad backspace), and
  `Icons.lock_outline` (PIN screen header), introducing no new icon package.

1	# Contract: `VaultRepository` (`lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart`)
2	
3	Domain-layer interface owning everything local to the device: PIN storage/verification, biometric
4	hardware capability, the local biometrics-preference mirror, and the in-memory relock timestamp.
5	`VaultBloc` and the lifecycle observer depend on this and on nothing in `vault/data/` directly
6	(RNF06). Registered as a `get_it` `lazySingleton` — one instance for the app's process lifetime,
7	which is what lets `lastUnlockedAt`/`backgroundedAt` survive navigation without a database
8	(data-model.md Vault Lock State).
9	
10	```dart
11	abstract class VaultRepository {
12	  // Device PIN
13	  Future<bool> hasPinConfigured();
14	  Future<void> savePin(String pin);          // hashes internally (research.md R2); overwrites any prior value
15	  Future<bool> verifyPin(String pin);         // hashes the input, compares to the stored digest
16	
17	  // Biometric capability (local_auth never crosses this boundary — see data-model.md)
18	  Future<BiometricCapability> checkBiometricCapability();
19	  Future<BiometricAuthOutcome> attemptBiometricAuth();   // success | failed | cancelled | notAvailable
20	
21	  // Local biometrics-preference mirror (NOT the backend's copy — research.md R6)
22	  Future<bool> isBiometricPreferenceEnabled();
23	  Future<void> setBiometricPreferenceLocally(bool enabled);
24	
25	  // Vault Lock State (in-memory only, data-model.md)
26	  void recordBackgrounded(DateTime at);
27	  DateTime? consumeBackgroundedAt();          // reads then clears, so one resume only ever evaluates once
28	  void markUnlocked(DateTime at);
29	  DateTime? get lastUnlockedAt;
30	}
31	```
32	
33	- **`hasPinConfigured`/`savePin`/`verifyPin`** → back `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`,
34	  `SavePinUseCase`, `VerifyPinUseCase`. None return `Either<Failure, T>` — research.md R5 covers
35	  why a local hash mismatch or "no PIN yet" is not a backend-taxonomy `Failure`.
36	- **`checkBiometricCapability`** → called once per `VaultPage` open (not cached across process
37	  lifetime, since the Edge Cases require detecting an OS-level biometric change *between*
38	  sessions — e.g. the user disabled Face ID in iOS Settings since the last launch).
39	- **`attemptBiometricAuth`** → wraps `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource.authenticate(biometricOnly:
40	  true)` (research.md R1); `cancelled` and `failed` are both routed to the same PIN-fallback UI by
41	  `VaultBloc` (FR-004 does not distinguish "not recognized" from "user tapped away").
42	- **`isBiometricPreferenceEnabled`/`setBiometricPreferenceLocally`** → the *local* mirror
43	  `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads; kept separate from `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`
44	  (which only ever writes to the backend, never reads) per research.md R6.
45	- **`recordBackgrounded`/`consumeBackgroundedAt`** → `VaultLifecycleObserver` calls these directly
46	  on pause/resume; `consumeBackgroundedAt` clears the stored value so a second rapid resume isn't
47	  double-counted against a background period that's already been evaluated.
48	- **`markUnlocked`/`lastUnlockedAt`** → `lastUnlockedAt` exists for observability/tests; the actual
49	  relock decision only needs `backgroundedAt` vs. "now" (data-model.md's
50	  `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`), not a comparison against `lastUnlockedAt` — the background
51	  gap itself is what's timed, not time-since-unlock, so a user who re-locks, re-unlocks, then
52	  backgrounds again immediately starts a fresh gap correctly.
53	
54	## `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` (orchestration, domain layer)
55	
56	```dart
57	Future<VaultEntryMode> call() async {
58	  if (!await repo.hasPinConfigured()) return VaultEntryMode.pinSetupRequired;
59	
60	  final capability = await repo.checkBiometricCapability();
61	  final preferred = await repo.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled();
62	  return (capability == BiometricCapability.available && preferred)
63	      ? VaultEntryMode.unlockBiometricFirst
64	      : VaultEntryMode.unlockPinOnly;
65	}
66	```
67	
68	This is the only place FR-003's "attempt biometrics first when enabled and available, otherwise go
69	straight to PIN" rule is implemented — `VaultBloc` calls it once per `VaultPage` open and never
70	re-derives the branching itself.
71	
72	## Who depends on this
73	
74	`VaultBloc` (both setup and unlock sub-states), `VaultLifecycleObserver` (background/resume
75	timing), `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` (writes the local mirror before firing the backend
76	call). No `presentation/` widget calls `VaultRepository` directly — always through a usecase or
77	through `VaultBloc`.

# Quickstart: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's four user stories. This
is a run guide, not an implementation spec — interfaces are in `contracts/`, state/entities in
`data-model.md`.

## Prerequisites

- F000 already implemented and passing (`specs/001-foundation/`) — RF03 builds directly on its
  `SessionBloc`/`AuthBloc`/`ApiClient`/`SecureTokenStorage`/routing.

- `ios/Runner/Info.plist` contains `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` (research.md R1) — without it, any
  call into `local_auth` on a real device or the Simulator crashes immediately, not just returns
  "unavailable."
- A `.env` with valid `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — only exercised by the one
  `account-settings-update` call (Story 3's optional biometrics opt-in); everything else in this
  unit works with no backend reachable at all (FR-002).

## Automated checks

```bash
fvm flutter analyze                                    # RNF06 import-shape lint (always_use_package_imports)
fvm flutter test --coverage
# RNF07 gate — same lcov filter F000 uses, now including lib/features/vault/domain
lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info
genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html   # inspect % manually, or script a threshold check
```

Key domain tests this unit's coverage depends on (contracts/vault-repository.md,
contracts/vault-lifecycle.md):
- `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`: exact-boundary cases (4:59 → false, 5:00 → true), `null`
  `backgroundedAt` → false.
- `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`: all four input combinations (no PIN; PIN + biometric available +
  preferred; PIN + biometric available + not preferred; PIN + biometric unavailable).
- `VerifyPinUseCase`/`SavePinUseCase` against a fake `VaultRepository`.
- `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`: the 3 failure scenarios in
  contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md.

## Manual verification (device/Simulator — `local_auth` has no platform channel under `flutter_test`)

The iOS Simulator supports Face ID without real hardware: **Features → Face ID → Enrolled**, then
**Features → Face ID → Matching Face** / **Non-matching Face** to simulate a pass/fail scan on
demand.

### Story 1 — Unlock with Face ID/Touch ID (P1)

1. Enroll Face ID in the Simulator; complete sign-up once (Story 3 flow below) with the biometric
   opt-in accepted.
2. Force-quit and relaunch the app (cold launch).
3. **Expect**: Splash → vault screen with the fingerprint prompt, before any Home/Chat content
   renders. **Features → Face ID → Matching Face** → app proceeds straight to Home/Chat.
4. Background the app (Simulator: Cmd+Shift+H or Device → Home), wait 5+ minutes (or temporarily
   lower the constant in a local-only debug build to verify the mechanism faster, then revert),
   bring it back. **Expect**: vault screen re-appears over Home/Chat; matching Face ID again
   reveals Home/Chat exactly as left (scroll position, any in-progress state).
5. Repeat the same background/resume but under 5 minutes. **Expect**: no vault screen, Home/Chat
   is immediately interactive.

### Story 2 — Biometric failure falls back to PIN (P1)

1. From the vault screen's fingerprint prompt, **Features → Face ID → Non-matching Face**.
2. **Expect**: PIN keypad appears immediately with "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN".
3. Enter the correct 4-digit PIN. **Expect**: unlocks normally.
4. Repeat; enter an incorrect PIN. **Expect**: digits clear, error state remains, no limit —
   retry with the correct PIN still works afterward.

### Story 3 — First-time PIN setup (P2)

1. Delete the app (or clear its Keychain data) to guarantee no PIN/session exists; launch fresh.
2. Sign up with a new email. **Expect**: immediately after signup succeeds, the create-PIN screen
   appears (not Home/Chat) — 4 progress dots, 3×4 keypad.
3. Enter 4 digits; **expect** the confirmation step. Enter a *different* 4 digits. **Expect**: clear
   mismatch message, returned to entering a new PIN, nothing saved yet.
4. Enter and confirm matching PINs. If the Simulator has Face ID enrolled, **expect** a biometrics
   opt-in prompt as part of this same flow; accept it.
5. **Expect**: proceeds to Home/Chat. Confirm in the backend (or a debug log of the request) that
   `PATCH account-settings-update` was called with `{"biometricEnabled": true}`.
6. Force-quit the Simulator mid-way through step 3 (after the first PIN entry, before
   confirmation) and relaunch. **Expect**: the PIN setup flow resumes (not a stuck/PIN-less state,
   not routed to Home/Chat).

### Story 4 — Recover via full login (P3)

1. From the vault screen (biometric or PIN state), tap "usar e-mail e senha".
2. **Expect**: the existing F000 login/sign-up screen opens.
3. Submit valid credentials. **Expect**: proceeds into the app the same way a fresh login would
   (i.e., through the vault gate again if a PIN is already configured on this device — see
   data-model.md's gatekeeper transition for `LoginSignupPage`'s success branch).

### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once

- Simulator **Features → Face ID → Enrolled** turned back off between launches → vault should show
  the PIN keypad directly on the next open, no fingerprint prompt attempted, no error about missing
  hardware.
- Offline device (Simulator network link conditioner, or airplane mode) during step 4–5 of Story
  3 → PIN setup still completes and reaches Home/Chat; only the backend write silently fails.

1	# Contract: `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`
2	(`lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/biometrics_preference_repository.dart`)
3	
4	Domain-layer interface for the one network call this unit makes. Deliberately narrow — a single
5	method for a single field — rather than a general-purpose account-settings repository; see "Why
6	this stays narrow" below.
7	
8	```dart
9	abstract class BiometricsPreferenceRepository {
10	  Future<Either<Failure, void>> save(bool enabled);   // PATCH account-settings-update, body: {biometricEnabled: enabled}
11	}
12	```
13	
14	- **`save`** → calls `ApiClient.call('account-settings-update', method: 'PATCH', body: {'biometricEnabled': enabled}, authMode: AuthMode.userSession)`, reusing F000's `ApiClient`/`ErrorMapper` unchanged. The OpenAPI schema for `account-settings-update` accepts `displayName`, `persona`, and `biometricEnabled` as independently-optional fields (`additionalProperties: false`, none individually `required`) — sending only `biometricEnabled` is a valid partial update, not a workaround.
15	- Return type is `Either<Failure, void>`, not `Either<Failure, Account>`: `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` (research.md R6) discards the result either way, so there is no reason to decode and carry the full updated-account payload the endpoint returns.
16	- **Caller discipline** (research.md R6, data-model.md Biometrics Preference): the caller always writes the local mirror *first*, then calls `save()` and ignores both branches of its `Either`. This repository itself does not know that — it is a plain, honestly-typed network call; the "don't block on failure" behavior lives one layer up, in the usecase, where it is independently testable without a fake clock or fake PIN state.
17	
18	## Data layer
19	
20	```dart
21	class BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource {
22	  BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource(this._apiClient);
23	  final ApiClient _apiClient;
24	
25	  Future<Either<Failure, Map<String, dynamic>>> update({required bool biometricEnabled}) =>
26	      _apiClient.call(
27	        'account-settings-update',
28	        method: 'PATCH',
29	        body: {'biometricEnabled': biometricEnabled},
30	      );
31	}
32	
33	class BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl implements BiometricsPreferenceRepository {
34	  BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl(this._remote);
35	  final BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource _remote;
36	
37	  @override
38	  Future<Either<Failure, void>> save(bool enabled) async =>
39	      (await _remote.update(biometricEnabled: enabled)).map((_) {});
40	}
41	```
42	
43	## Test scenarios (contributes toward RNF09's 15/15, data-model.md Backend Failure)
44	
45	Covered with `mocktail` against `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl` (mocking `ApiClient`, matching
46	F000's `auth_repository_impl_test.dart` pattern exactly):
47	
48	1. `ApiClient.call` returns `Right({...})` → `save()` returns `Right(unit)`.
49	2. `ApiClient.call` returns `Left(NetworkTimeoutFailure(...))` → `save()` returns the same `Left` unchanged.
50	3. `ApiClient.call` returns `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure(...))` → `save()` returns the same `Left` unchanged.
51	4. `ApiClient.call` returns `Left(ValidationFailure(...))` → `save()` returns the same `Left` unchanged (malformed-response case).
52	
53	## Why this stays narrow
54	
55	FR-016 bars this unit from building any part of the Settings screen; spec.md's Assumptions say a
56	"dedicated toggle to change the biometrics preference later... belongs to the Settings screen built
57	by the RF09 unit." A general `AccountRepository.updateSettings({displayName, persona,
58	biometricEnabled})` would anticipate that unit's needs (`displayName`/`persona` editing) without
59	being asked to — the opposite problem from F000's `Failure` hierarchy, where going wide *was*
60	correct because the error taxonomy is closed and fully known today (F000 research.md R6). Here,
61	RF09's actual settings-screen shape isn't known yet, so the narrow interface is the version that
62	can be reused or widened later without this unit having guessed wrong.
63

1	# Contract: Background-resume relock (`VaultLifecycleObserver` + `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`)
2	
3	Covers FR-007–FR-010 and User Story 1's background-resume scenarios, plus the Edge Cases'
4	"process killed while backgrounded" and "exactly at the 5-minute boundary" cases. This is the
5	mechanism that is independent of which screen (`VaultPage` included) happens to be on top when the
6	app backgrounds.
7	
8	## `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase` (domain layer, pure)
9	
10	```dart
11	class EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase {
12	  const EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase();
13	
14	  static const backgroundTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);   // FR-009 — the ONLY place this constant is defined
15	
16	  bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
17	    if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
18	    return !resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt).isNegative &&
19	        resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= backgroundTimeout;
20	  }
21	}
22	```
23	
24	- No I/O, no `package:flutter` import, no settings read — testable with plain `DateTime` literals,
25	  including the exact-boundary case the Edge Cases call out ("fewer than 5 minutes elapsed never
26	  re-prompts; 5 minutes or more always does") as a direct unit test:
27	  `call(backgroundedAt: t, resumedAt: t.add(Duration(minutes: 5)))` must be `true`;
28	  `t.add(Duration(minutes: 4, seconds: 59))` must be `false`.
29	- `backgroundTimeout` lives here, not as a `VaultRepository` field or a `VaultBloc` constant — one
30	  definition, referenced by tests and (if ever needed) by presentation, never duplicated.
31	
32	## `VaultLifecycleObserver` (presentation layer, `WidgetsBindingObserver`)
33	
34	```dart
35	class VaultLifecycleObserver extends StatefulWidget {
36	  const VaultLifecycleObserver({required this.child, super.key});
37	  final Widget child;
38	  // ...
39	}
40	
41	class _VaultLifecycleObserverState extends State<VaultLifecycleObserver>
42	    with WidgetsBindingObserver {
43	  @override
44	  void didChangeAppLifecycleState(AppLifecycleState state) {
45	    final repo = getIt<VaultRepository>();
46	    switch (state) {
47	      case AppLifecycleState.paused:
48	        repo.recordBackgrounded(DateTime.now());
49	      case AppLifecycleState.resumed:
50	        final backgroundedAt = repo.consumeBackgroundedAt();
51	        final shouldRelock = const EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase()
52	            .call(backgroundedAt: backgroundedAt, resumedAt: DateTime.now());
53	        if (shouldRelock && repo.lastUnlockedAt != null) {
54	          rootNavigatorKey.currentState!.push(
55	            MaterialPageRoute<void>(
56	              builder: (_) => BlocProvider<VaultBloc>(
57	                create: (_) => getIt<VaultBloc>(),
58	                child: const VaultPage(mode: VaultMode.relock),
59	              ),
60	            ),
61	          );
62	        }
63	      default:
64	        break;
65	    }
66	  }
67	}
68	```
69	
70	- **`repo.lastUnlockedAt != null` guard** — a relock push only ever makes sense once the vault has
71	  actually been passed at least once this process. Without this guard, backgrounding the app while
72	  still sitting on `LoginSignupPage` (unauthenticated, no session, nothing to protect yet) could
73	  spuriously push a vault screen with nothing underneath worth protecting. This mirrors
74	  `SessionBloc._onAuthExpiredDetected`'s own re-entrancy guard
75	  (`if (state is SessionStatusExpiredRenewable) return;`) — both exist to stop a cross-cutting
76	  observer from firing when its precondition screen isn't actually the one in front.
77	- Installed exactly once, in `main.dart`, wrapping `MaterialApp.router`'s `builder` child — the
78	  same spot the existing session-expired `BlocListener` already wraps (`main.dart`, current
79	  `CerneApp.build`). Both can coexist in the same `builder` without interacting: a `VaultPage`
80	  relock push and a `showSessionExpiredOverlay` dialog push are independent root-navigator
81	  pushes, and neither depends on the other's state.
82	- Not testable with `flutter_test`'s widget tests in the way `bloc_test` tests
83	  `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase` — `WidgetsBindingObserver` lifecycle callbacks can be
84	  simulated via `tester.binding.handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(...)` in a widget test; that test
85	  belongs to `tasks.md`, not this plan.
86	
87	## Who depends on this
88	
89	Nothing in `domain/` or `data/` depends on `VaultLifecycleObserver` — it is purely a
90	presentation-layer wiring point that calls two already-contracted `VaultRepository` methods and
91	one pure usecase. `main.dart` is the only call site.
92

# Data Model: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

Source: spec.md §Key Entities, requirements.md §§1, 6.1, 10, prototype-extract.md §§2.1, 3.
Entities here are either on-device-only domain objects (Device PIN, Vault Lock State) or a local
mirror of one backend field (Biometrics Preference) — this unit introduces no new backend table
and no new local database (just two new secure-storage keys alongside F000's four).

## Device PIN

A 4-digit secret, created once (User Story 3) and checked on every subsequent unlock attempt
(User Stories 1–2). Never transmitted to, or validated by, the backend (FR-002).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pinHash` | `String` (hex, sha256) | Written by `VaultSecureStorage`; see research.md R2 for why the raw digit string is never the thing stored. |

**Validation rule**: exactly 4 digits, each `0`–`9`, no partial/shorter value ever written or
compared (FR-005). Confirmation during setup is a pure string-equality check between two freshly
entered 4-digit values — the first one is held only in memory (`VaultState`) between entry and
confirmation, never written to storage until it matches (FR-012: "without the mismatched PIN being
saved").

## Vault Lock State

Whether the current app process currently requires authentication before showing data, and when it
was last satisfied — the input to the 5-minute background-resume rule (FR-007–FR-010).

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `lastUnlockedAt` | `DateTime?` | In-memory only, held by the `VaultRepository` singleton (one instance for the app's lifetime via `get_it`'s `registerLazySingleton`). `null` until the first successful unlock this process. Never persisted to disk — see research.md R3 for why a killed/relaunched process doesn't need this to survive. |
| `backgroundedAt` | `DateTime?` | Set by `VaultLifecycleObserver` on `AppLifecycleState.paused`; read and cleared on the matching `.resumed`. In-memory only, same lifetime as `lastUnlockedAt`. |

**Derived decision — `VaultEntryMode`** (domain enum/sealed type, computed by
`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` every time `VaultPage` opens):

```
pinSetupRequired                      # hasPinConfigured() == false
unlockBiometricFirst                  # PIN exists AND biometric capability == available
                                       #   AND the local biometrics-preference mirror == true
unlockPinOnly                         # PIN exists AND (no biometric capability OR preference == false)
```

**State transitions**:

```
[SplashPage, SessionStatusAuthenticated]  or  [LoginSignupPage, AuthStatus.authenticated (non-reauth)]
  context.push(AppRoutes.vault)   # mode: gatekeeper
      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()
          pinSetupRequired      -> show "Digite seu PIN" (new) -> confirm -> [optional] offer biometrics
                                     -> on complete: context.go(AppRoutes.home)     (Story 3)
          unlockBiometricFirst  -> auto-trigger local_auth prompt
              success            -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)   (Story 1)
              failed/cancelled   -> show "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" + PIN keypad (Story 2)
                  correct PIN      -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)
                  incorrect PIN    -> clear digits, keep error banner, no lockout, retry allowed (Story 2, Edge Cases)
          unlockPinOnly          -> show PIN keypad directly, no biometric prompt attempted (Edge Cases: no hardware/not enrolled/OS-disabled)
      at any point: "usar e-mail e senha" -> context.push(AppRoutes.login)          (Story 4)

[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == true]
  rootNavigatorKey.push(VaultPage)   # mode: relock — pushed OVER whatever screen is current
      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()   # always unlockBiometricFirst or unlockPinOnly — PIN already exists
          success (biometric or PIN)  -> markUnlocked() -> Navigator.pop()   # reveals the preserved screen underneath, state untouched

[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == false]
  no-op — screen underneath was never covered, no re-authentication required   (FR-008)
```

**Fixed rule** (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`, FR-009):

```dart
bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
  if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
  return resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= const Duration(minutes: 5);
}
```

A pure function of two timestamps and one constant — no settings read, no parameter — is itself
the mechanism by which FR-009's "fixed value, not configurable by the user" is enforced.

## Biometrics Preference

An account-level flag indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's chosen unlock method —
read locally at every vault entry to decide `unlockBiometricFirst` vs. `unlockPinOnly`, and mirrored
to the backend for durability/future display (RF09's Settings screen), per FR-013.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `biometricPreferenceLocal` | `bool` | Written to `VaultSecureStorage` during first-time PIN setup (Story 3, scenario 4) if the user opts in; this is the value `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads at runtime — never the backend's copy (research.md R6). Defaults to `false` until set. |
| `biometricEnabled` (remote) | `bool` | The backend's `users.biometric_enabled` field (requirements.md §8), read/written only through `PATCH /account/settings` → `account-settings-update`. This unit only ever **writes** it (fire-and-forget, FR-014); it never reads it back. |

**Write path** (`SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, FR-013/FR-014):

```
1. VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)        # synchronous, always succeeds (local write)
2. BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)                  # await, discard Either<Failure, T> result
3. proceed to Home/Chat regardless of step 2's outcome            # Clarifications; Edge Cases
```

## Backend Failure (reused, not redefined)

`BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` is the only network call this unit makes; it returns
`Either<Failure, T>` using F000's existing `core/network/failure.dart` hierarchy unchanged (no new
`Failure` subtype — research.md R5). The three scenarios covered by this unit's own tests, toward
RNF09's 15-scenario total:

| Scenario | Expected `Failure` | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| Request exceeds the timeout | `NetworkTimeoutFailure` | yes |
| No connection at all | `NetworkOfflineFailure` | yes |
| Malformed response body | `ValidationFailure` | no |

None of these three block the PIN-setup-complete transition (R6) — they are observed only by this
unit's own `mocktail` tests of `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`, never surfaced to the user.

## Biometric Capability (domain enum, no `local_auth` type crosses into `domain/`)

```
available        # canCheckBiometrics && isDeviceSupported && getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty
noHardware        # isDeviceSupported == false
notEnrolled        # hardware present, nothing enrolled at the OS level
osDisabled        # was available in a previous session, no longer (Edge Cases: OS-level disable between sessions)
```

`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` (data layer) is the only place that imports `local_auth`'s own
types (`LocalAuthentication`, `AuthenticationOptions`, `BiometricType`); `VaultRepositoryImpl` maps
its result into this enum before it ever reaches `domain/` or `presentation/` (RNF06).

## Presentation-only state (not persisted, not a domain entity)

- **`VaultMode`** (`gatekeeper | relock`) — which of the two entry points opened `VaultPage`;
  decides `go(home)` vs. `pop()` on success (data-model.md State transitions above). Passed as a
  constructor parameter, not stored anywhere.
- **First-entry PIN held during confirmation** — the first 4-digit value typed during first-time
  setup, kept only in `VaultBloc`'s in-memory state until the confirmation entry either matches
  (written to storage) or doesn't (discarded, user restarts entry — FR-012).
- **PIN-entry digit buffer / progress-dot count** — transient widget/bloc state for the keypad,
  reset to empty after every failed attempt (Edge Cases: "the entered digits are cleared").

## Design Tokens (`lib/core/design_tokens.dart`) — additions only

Every color, type style, spacing, and radius the vault screens use already exists from F000
(`colorPrimary`, `colorOnPrimary`, `colorError`, `colorSurfaceBg`, `textHeadlineMd`, `textBodyMd`,
`textTitleSm`, `spacing*`, `radius*`). One value is new, per research.md R7:

| Token | Value | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `sizeKeypadTapTarget` | `72` (double, dp) | `pin_keypad.dart` — the circular tap target for each of the 12 keys (digits 0–9 + backspace + the empty 4th-row-left cell), per the prototype's "3×4 numeric keypad" with no explicit pixel size given. |

No other component-level token (spine colors, sync badge, bookmark states, etc.) is needed — those
belong to later units' own screens, same precedent F000's data-model.md already set.
